happy_path.title: Large 2xx JSON webhook response no longer stalls — processPayload completes promptly and reaches archival/success
happy_path.preconditions: Isolated offline harness in acmeclose-openfaas/webhook-delivery with the committed node-fetch 2.x resolution; a local HTTP receiver under the harness's control (never a production receiver or queue); synthetic payload data only.
steps: Start a local HTTP server that responds HTTP 200 with a finite synthetic JSON body well above node-fetch's clone stream high-water mark (e.g. ~64 KB of repeated synthetic ASCII; the stall threshold reported in the PR is roughly 16 KB).

Require `processPayload` from `utils/request-processor.js` (now exported) and invoke it with a synthetic payload whose `targetUrl` points at the local server, a non-legacy (JSON) payload type, and a stub logger that records calls.
Impose a short harness deadline (e.g. 5 s) that is far below the 60 s node-fetch timeout.
Assert the promise resolves before the harness deadline.
happy_path.expected: `processPayload` resolves within the short harness deadline — it reads the body once via `response.text()` with no un-consumed clone branch, so no backpressure stall occurs and the delivery proceeds to the archive move / success path instead of timing out at 60 s and being marked failed (424) and retried.
happy_path.test_data: Local receiver: HTTP 200, Content-Type application/json, synthetic body ≈64 KB (> ~16 KB tee buffer). Harness deadline 5 s (< 60 s node-fetch timeout). No real customer or transaction data.
happy_path.credentials: none — offline unit/integration harness against a localhost receiver; no AWS, queue, or production credentials.
happy_path.environment: Local developer / CI harness — acmeclose-openfaas repo, `webhook-delivery` function, `__tests__/request-processor.unit.js`
happy_path.unit_test_ref: __tests__/request-processor.unit.js › large-body suite (real node-fetch Response streaming a large body, per PR #5 description)

happy_path.title: Large 2xx SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML success response is fully read and parsed (full body, not the excerpt)
happy_path.preconditions: Same offline harness as above; synthetic XML only.
steps: Start a local HTTP server returning HTTP 200 with a synthetic SOFTPRO legacy XML body whose total length exceeds ~16 KB and whose `<success>` element — placed AFTER more than 256 characters of filler — indicates success.
Call `processPayload` with a synthetic payload of type `SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML` targeting that server and a stub logger.
Assert the call resolves without throwing, within a short harness deadline.
Inspect the stub logger's recorded info entry.
happy_path.expected: The call resolves successfully: XML success parsing reads the COMPLETE response body (not the 256-character excerpt), so a success flag located beyond character 256 is still detected. No error is thrown and no 60 s stall occurs.
happy_path.test_data: Synthetic legacy XML ≈20 KB with >256 chars of filler preceding the success element. No real transaction data.
happy_path.expected_source: utils/request-processor.js:156 (`const xmlBodyAsJson = await parseXMLBody(responseText);` — full body, not the excerpt)
happy_path.unit_test_ref: __tests__/request-processor.unit.js › large XML success suite (per PR #5 description: 'regression tests cover large bodies plus legacy XML failure handling')

happy_path.title: Delivery log carries a 256-character excerpt plus responseBytes, and preserves verb/url/code
happy_path.preconditions: Offline harness; stub logger capturing the object passed to logger.info.
steps: Call `processPayload` with a synthetic payload whose receiver returns HTTP 200 with a synthetic body longer than 256 characters.
Capture the object passed to `logger.info`.
Assert the `resp` field length and content.
Assert `responseBytes` equals the byte length of the FULL body, not the excerpt length.
Assert `verb`, `url` and `code` are still present and correct.
happy_path.expected: `logger.info` receives `resp` = the first 256 characters of the body followed by the truncation marker (257 characters total), `responseBytes` = Buffer.byteLength of the full untruncated body, and the pre-existing fields `verb` (payload.method), `url` (encodeURI of targetUrl) and `code` (response.status) unchanged.
happy_path.test_data: Synthetic ASCII body of 1,000 characters → expected resp length 257 (256 + marker), responseBytes 1000. No real response bodies.
happy_path.expected_source: utils/request-processor.js:150-155 (`resp: responseExcerpt(responseText), responseBytes: Buffer.byteLength(responseText)`), with RESPONSE_EXCERPT_CHARS = 256 at :97
happy_path.unit_test_ref: __tests__/request-processor.unit.js › truncation / byte-length / preserved log fields (verb, url, code) cases (per PR #6 summary)

happy_path.title: Ordinary small 2xx webhook delivery is unchanged end-to-end
happy_path.preconditions: Offline harness with a mocked response object.
steps: Call `processPayload` with a synthetic payload whose receiver returns HTTP 200 with a short synthetic body (under 256 characters).
Capture the logger.info object and the resolution of the call.
happy_path.expected: The call resolves; `resp` contains the body verbatim with NO truncation marker appended; `responseBytes` equals the body's byte length; `verb`, `url`, `code` are logged as before. Behaviour for ordinary small responses is identical to pre-change behaviour.
happy_path.expected_source: utils/request-processor.js:99-101 (responseExcerpt returns text unchanged when length <= 256)

edge_cases.title: Exploit path proof: an unread clone branch stalls, the shipped single-read path does not (negative control)
edge_cases.preconditions: Offline harness using the committed node-fetch 2.x resolution; local receiver only — never a production receiver or queue.
steps: Start a local HTTP server returning HTTP 200 with a finite synthetic body larger than node-fetch's clone stream high-water mark (≈64 KB).
EXPLOIT CONTROL: in harness code only (not production code), fetch the URL and call `response.clone().text()` without reading `response.body`; apply a 5 s harness deadline.
Assert that this clone-only read does NOT complete within the deadline.
FIXED PATH: call the shipped `processPayload` against the same receiver with the same 5 s deadline.
Assert the shipped path completes within the deadline.
edge_cases.expected: The clone-only read (the pre-fix shape) does not resolve within 5 s, demonstrating the backpressure stall; the shipped `processPayload` — which reads `response.text()` once — resolves within 5 s. This is the regression test the ticket's 'Done when' requires (exploit path plus negative case).
edge_cases.test_data: Synthetic body ≈64 KB; harness deadline 5 s; node-fetch pinned at the committed 2.x resolution (yarn.lock). No production data.
edge_cases.expected_source: utils/request-processor.js:140 (single `await response.text()`; the clone call is gone)

data_shape.shape: An HTTP 200 response whose body exceeds node-fetch 2.x's clone stream high-water mark (~16 KB) and is finite.
data_shape.evidence: No live receiver in the repo is documented as returning bodies of this size, and the ticket explicitly forbids using a production receiver. The PR itself used 'a real node-fetch Response streaming a large body' inside the test suite.
data_shape.obtain: Engineering stands up a local HTTP server (or a real node-fetch Response over a synthetic stream) in `__tests__/request-processor.unit.js` that emits ≈64 KB of synthetic ASCII under a 200 status. QA cannot produce this from any UI.

edge_cases.expected_source_unconfirmed_reason: cites a file but no line number

edge_cases.title: SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML bad response: error message carries only the bounded excerpt, never the full body
steps: Have the mocked receiver return HTTP 200 with a synthetic legacy XML body whose success element is false/absent AND whose total length far exceeds 256 characters (e.g. ~10 KB of synthetic filler).
Call `processPayload` with payload type `SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML` and capture the thrown error.
Measure the length of the error message and compare the body portion against the original body.
edge_cases.expected: An Error is thrown whose message names the method and target URL and embeds only the 256-character excerpt (with the truncation marker) — the full ~10 KB body does NOT appear in the error text. The excerpt in the error is identical to the one written to the log.
edge_cases.test_data: Synthetic failing XML ≈10 KB. Expected embedded body portion = 257 characters (256 + marker).
edge_cases.unit_test_ref: __tests__/request-processor.unit.js › 'oversized failure payloads are not embedded in error text' (per PR #6 summary)
edge_cases.expected_source_unconfirmed_reason: cites a file but no line number

edge_cases.title: Multi-byte response body: excerpt is counted in characters, responseBytes in bytes
steps: Have the mocked receiver return HTTP 200 with a synthetic body composed of multi-byte characters (e.g. 500 identical non-ASCII characters) so byte length differs from character length.
Call `processPayload` and capture the logger.info object.
Compare the character length of `resp` against `responseBytes`.
edge_cases.expected: `resp` is 256 characters plus the truncation marker (character-based slice, no split surrogate garbage in the common case), while `responseBytes` reports the FULL body's byte length computed with Buffer.byteLength — a larger number than the character count. The two values are deliberately different units and must not be conflated.
edge_cases.test_data: 500 multi-byte characters (e.g. a repeated 3-byte UTF-8 character) → character length 500, byte length 1500; expected resp length 257, responseBytes 1500.
edge_cases.expected_source: utils/request-processor.js:99-101 and :154 (slice by chars; Buffer.byteLength for bytes)
edge_cases.unit_test_ref: __tests__/request-processor.unit.js › byte-length accounting including multi-byte characters (per PR #6 summary)

edge_cases.title: Truncation boundary: exactly 256 characters is not marked truncated; 257 is
steps: Call `processPayload` with a mocked 200 response whose body is exactly 256 ASCII characters; capture logger.info.
Repeat with a body of exactly 257 ASCII characters; capture logger.info.
Compare both `resp` values against the respective source bodies.
edge_cases.expected: For the 256-character body, `resp` equals the body verbatim with NO truncation marker (the helper truncates only when length is strictly greater than 256) and responseBytes = 256. For the 257-character body, `resp` is the first 256 characters plus the truncation marker (257 characters) and responseBytes = 257.
edge_cases.test_data:
| Body length | Expected resp | Expected responseBytes |
|---|---|---|
| 256 ASCII chars | body verbatim, no marker | 256 |
| 257 ASCII chars | first 256 chars + marker | 257 |

edge_cases.title: Empty 2xx response body does not break logging or legacy XML handling
steps: Call `processPayload` with a mocked 200 response whose body is an empty string, using a non-legacy JSON payload type; capture logger.info.
Repeat with payload type `SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML` and capture the outcome.
edge_cases.expected: For the JSON type, the call resolves; `resp` is the empty string (no marker) and `responseBytes` is 0. For the legacy XML type, the existing XML-parse failure path is exercised — unverified: the diff does not change how parseXMLBody handles an empty string, so record whatever the current behaviour is (reject/throw) and confirm it is unchanged from pre-fix behaviour rather than newly introduced.

edge_cases.title: Inverse trigger: a large body no longer converts an accepted delivery into a failed/retried one
edge_cases.preconditions: Offline harness with the delivery outcome observable (resolution vs. thrown body-timeout).
steps: Start a local receiver returning HTTP 200 with a synthetic body ≈64 KB for a non-legacy JSON payload type.
Call `processPayload` under a harness deadline shorter than the 60 s node-fetch timeout.
Assert the call resolves rather than rejecting with a body-timeout error.
Assert the stub logger records no delivery-failure path for this invocation.
edge_cases.expected: No body-timeout rejection occurs. The accepted 2xx is treated as a success, so the downstream failed/retry (424 + DLQ, per the kickoff comment) path is NOT entered — this is the duplicate-send side effect the fix removes.
edge_cases.test_data: Synthetic 64 KB 200 body; harness deadline 5 s; node-fetch timeout 60 s default (utils/http.js).
edge_cases.expected_source: utils/request-processor.js:140 — single read removes the tee stall that previously produced the body timeout
edge_cases.expected_source_unconfirmed_reason: cites a file but no line number

steps: From the repo root, run the new mocked suite `__tests__/request-processor.unit.js` with network egress blocked (e.g. offline mode or a blocking proxy).

Confirm the pre-existing `__tests__/request-processor.js` suite (which the kickoff comment says hits live AWS/httpbin) remains a separate file and is not required for this suite to pass.

integration_tests.title: [Backend] node-fetch stays on the committed 2.x line after the open Dependabot bump
steps: Check out the Dependabot dependency-bump PR branch (PR #1, open at time of kickoff).
Resolve the installed node-fetch version for the `webhook-delivery` function and for the root lockfile.
Compare the resolved major version against the committed 2.x resolution.
If node-fetch has moved to a 3.x line, re-run the large-body suite and record the outcome.
integration_tests.expected: node-fetch remains on the 2.x line that `webhook-delivery/package.json` declares and the root lockfile resolves. If the bump moves it to a 3.x major, flag it before merge — the body-read semantics and the `timeout` option behaviour differ, and the regression suite must be re-validated against the new major.
integration_tests.test_data: Compare `webhook-delivery/package.json` dependency range against the resolved lockfile entry.

regression_checklist: 🔴 A SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML delivery whose success flag appears BEYOND character 256 of the body still parses as success — XML parsing must use the full body, never the 256-character excerpt (utils/request-processor.js:156).
🔴 A SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML delivery with a failing success flag still throws and is still treated as a failed delivery — the excerpt change must not swallow the failure, only shorten its message.
🔴 Ordinary small-body 2xx deliveries (under 256 characters) complete and log `resp` verbatim with no truncation marker — unchanged from pre-fix behaviour.
🔴 Non-2xx receiver responses are still rejected by `sendRequest` in utils/http.js and never reach the success/archive path — the response-read change must not alter status handling.

🔴 Exploit regression: with the committed node-fetch 2.x resolution, a 200 response larger than the clone high-water mark completes inside a short harness deadline; the clone-only control in the same harness still stalls (proves the fix, not the harness).

🟡 The delivery log entry still carries `verb`, `url` (encodeURI of targetUrl) and `code` alongside the new `resp` excerpt and `responseBytes`; downstream log consumers/dashboards that read these fields are unaffected.
🟡 Any log search or alert that previously matched on the full `resp` body content is reviewed — bodies are now truncated at 256 characters, so content beyond that no longer appears in logs.

🟡 Run the new offline mocked suite `__tests__/request-processor.unit.js` with network egress blocked and confirm it passes without AWS or httpbin, keeping it independent of the live-network `__tests__/request-processor.js` suite.

🟡 Re-run the full webhook-delivery test suite on the Dependabot dependency-bump branch and confirm node-fetch has not moved off the 2.x line; if it has, re-validate the large-body behaviour before merging either PR.

🟡 Bounce-back re-walk (Ready for UAT → In Progress, 2026-10-09, reason unrecorded): execute the complete delivery flow once end-to-end on a non-prod deployment with a disposable receiver returning a large 200 body — invoke, deliver, archive, success callback — and confirm no stall, no 424/retry, and no duplicate send. The earlier bounce had no recorded reason, so walk the whole flow rather than a single assertion.

🟢 Deploy-time sanity on the non-prod `webhook-delivery` pod: the startup probe on /_/health passes and the pod does not enter CrashLoopBackOff after the redeploy that ships this change (README deployment notes).
🟢 Memory behaviour of the function under a large (multi-MB) receiver response is observed at least once against the 256Mi limit / 192MB heap cap, since no response-byte cap was added in this change.

risks_and_gaps.gap: No response-byte cap was added. The Audit finding's 'apply an explicit byte limit' and node-fetch `size` option recommendations were explicitly deferred to a follow-up in PR #5's description, and `utils/http.js` still passes a timeout but no `size` option to node-fetch.
risks_and_gaps.impact: A hostile receiver can still force the worker to buffer an arbitrarily large 2xx body into a JavaScript string. With the container capped at 256Mi and the V8 heap at 192MB, a sufficiently large response can exhaust memory or inflate per-invocation time even though the 60 s tee stall is gone — the CWE-400 resource-exhaustion class is reduced, not closed.
risks_and_gaps.evidence: utils/http.js:7-27 (timeout only, no size option) plus PR #5 description: 'The size-cap and bounded log-excerpt suggestions from the Audit finding are intentionally left for a follow-up.'

risks_and_gaps.gap: No total job/response concurrency bound was introduced, which the finding calls out as a missing control ('the code defines no total job concurrency or response-byte bound').
risks_and_gaps.impact: Repeated slow-but-legal large responses can still occupy concurrent worker slots and build queue lag, though for a much shorter window now that deliveries no longer hang for the full 60 s timeout.
risks_and_gaps.evidence: Ticket description, 'Why current controls do not stop it'; neither PR diff touches concurrency configuration.

risks_and_gaps.gap: The ticket's 'Done when' requires that a Audit rerun no longer reports fingerprint `acmeclose-openfaas|CWE-400|utils/request-processor.js|unconsumed-response-clone-stalls-delivery`, but nothing in the development activity records that rerun.
risks_and_gaps.impact: The ticket can be closed while the audit still reports the fingerprint, since the byte-limit half of 'What to change' was deferred; sign-off may be premature.
risks_and_gaps.evidence: Ticket 'Done when' bullet 4; no commit, PR, or comment references a Audit rerun result.

risks_and_gaps.gap: The pre-existing suite `__tests__/request-processor.js` is described in the kickoff comment as hitting live AWS/httpbin, and neither PR changes it.
risks_and_gaps.impact: CI for this function remains partly dependent on external services; a network or httpbin outage can mask or falsely fail the regression coverage that proves this fix.
risks_and_gaps.evidence: Jira comment by Dev Agent, 2026-10-08: 'the existing __tests__/request-processor.js hits live AWS/httpbin, so add a separate mocked suite.'

needs_spec_cases.title: No response-byte cap exists — an unbounded (very large) 2xx body is still read in full
steps: Start a local receiver returning HTTP 200 with a synthetic body substantially larger than any realistic receiver reply (e.g. 50 MB of synthetic ASCII).
Call `processPayload` under a generous harness deadline and observe memory/time.
Record whether the body is read in full into a string.

This case documents residual exposure, not a defect of the shipped change; do not file it as a bug against this ticket.

needs_spec_cases.title: [Backend] End-to-end webhook delivery against a non-production receiver completes, archives, and logs the bounded excerpt
needs_spec_cases.preconditions: A non-production deployment of the `webhook-delivery` function wired to a disposable test receiver and a disposable archive bucket/queue. Blocked until a deployed non-prod environment with the merged branch exists, owner: the team that owns the webhook-delivery deployment. Use synthetic payloads only — never a production receiver or queue.
steps: Point a synthetic accepted webhook payload at a disposable receiver that replies HTTP 200 with a synthetic body of roughly 64 KB.
Invoke the deployed function with that payload.
Watch the function's logs for the delivery entry.
Check that the payload object is moved to the archive location and the success callback is made.
needs_spec_cases.expected: The invocation completes well inside the 60 s node-fetch timeout, the archive move and success callback occur, and the log entry for the delivery shows a `resp` field truncated to a 256-character excerpt with the truncation marker plus a `responseBytes` field carrying the full ~64 KB byte count. No retry or DLQ entry is produced for this delivery.
